title: NSW plan to cut $11b debt
full_text:
The NSW government will overhaul how the state manages its long-term superannuation liabilities as part of an $11 billion debt reduction plan designed to lower state borrowings.
The bulk of the money will come from redirecting dividends NSW receives from its remaining equity stakes in electricity distributors Ausgrid and Endeavour Energy directly into the General Government Liability Management Fund, which is the state's primary superannuation investment vehicle.
NSW Treasurer Daniel Mookhey intends to use the funds to partly trim the annual state borrowings by an average $1.2 billion, adding up to $11 billion less borrowed over the next decade.
The proposals will form a pillar of Labor's economic platform as the political parties outline their fiscal frameworks ahead of a March election.
The NSW government in its 2026-2027 budget projected it would receive more than $614 million for that financial year from the combined dividends of their stake in Ausgrid and Endeavour. The rest would need to be made up by finance from the state's central investment platform OneFund.
"Every dollar we don't pay our bondholders in interest is a dollar we can invest in the roads, schools, hospitals and public transport, which makes life more affordable for working families," Mookhey said.
